Chapter 9: Goodness and Mercy—The Companions of the Journey.
As the days pass and the seasons change, two quiet companions always walk with the flock—goodness and mercy.
They’re not loud, they don’t grab your attention, but you can feel their presence all the same. The shepherd’s care goes way beyond just meeting needs in the moment—it’s about shaping a life that’s marked by these simple, powerful gifts.
Can you picture it? The flock makes its way through rolling hills, sometimes following twisting paths that climb and dip. The shepherd leads from the front, guiding the way. But right behind, goodness and mercy follow. They gather up anyone who’s fallen back, look after the tired ones, and make absolutely sure that no one ever gets left behind.
Their presence is a promise—no matter what the journey looks like, these gifts won’t ever leave you.
Now, a lot of us think of goodness and mercy as something far off—maybe only for the lucky, or for those who seem to have it all together. But here’s what’s different about the shepherd’s way: goodness isn’t something you earn, it’s something you receive. And mercy? It’s not a reward for being perfect. It’s a gift—especially for those of us who stumble along the way.
This journey isn’t about proving you’re worthy. It’s about accepting what’s freely offered.
Imagine one morning, a sheep starts to lag behind—tired, discouraged. Goodness gently nudges it forward, maybe with a patch of sweet, fresh grass to lift its spirits. Mercy lingers close, patient and kind, waiting until the sheep finds its strength again. The flock keeps moving, but no one gets left out or forgotten.
It’s these small acts of care, repeated over and over, that really mark the journey.
Most people, honestly, underestimate the power of these companions. In a world that prizes achievement and going it alone, goodness and mercy can seem almost unnecessary—maybe even weak. But the shepherd knows better. These gifts? They’re the foundation of the flock’s well-being, the glue that keeps the whole community together.
Over time, the sheep learn to trust these companions. They start to expect kindness, to lean on forgiveness, and to rest in the comfort that they’re never alone. Sure, the path can still be tough, but it’s softened by the steady presence of goodness and mercy. The flock becomes a true place of safety—a community where every single member is valued and cared for.
So, if you’ve ever longed for a different way of living, the picture of goodness and mercy is a real invitation. There’s room here for every failure, every weakness, every need. The shepherd’s care isn’t about judgment—it’s about grace.
And this journey? It’s not about earning love. It’s about receiving it, day after day.
